movement_source: row 'Net interest margin (%)', column 30 Jun 20 full year column -> column 30 Jun 21 full year column
headline: CBA's Group net interest margin (continuing operations, cash basis) fell 4bpts to 2.03% in FY21 from 2.07% in FY20 (ev-24, ev-1). Including discontinued operations the same KPI table prints 2.03% vs 2.08%, a 5bpt decline (ev-25); the FY20 book had reported FY20 continuing-operations NIM at 2.07%, so the comparator is unrestated (ev-30). Net interest income still rose $229m or 1% to $18,839m, as a $32bn/4% rise in average interest earning assets to $930bn outweighed the margin fall (ev-2). The bank frames the decline as almost entirely liquids-driven: margin was "Flat ex liquids – pressure from lower interest rates, offset by favourable portfolio mix, lower wholesale funding costs", with the higher-liquids bar carrying "Minimal impact on NII" (ev-27, ev-12). The seven-bar walk (liquids -4, asset pricing -2, deposit pricing & funding -3, capital & other -2, portfolio mix +2, basis risk +3, Treasury & Markets +2) sums exactly to -4bpts (ev-11).

drivers.columns: FY20 vs FY21 (30 Jun 20 vs 30 Jun 21)
drivers.narrative: Largest drag: "increased lower yielding non-lending interest earning assets, including liquid assets" (ev-3). Non-lending average balances rose 12% to $195bn, driven by a $17bn rise in average liquid assets on strong customer deposit growth (ev-6). The slide flags "Minimal impact on NII" — dilution, not lost income (ev-12).

drivers.columns: FY20 vs FY21 (30 Jun 20 vs 30 Jun 21)
drivers.narrative: Net -3bpts: lower earnings on transaction and savings deposits "mainly due to decreases in the cash rate" (-7bpts; slide prints -8) partly offset by higher replicating portfolio benefits (+2bpts) and lower wholesale funding costs (+2bpts) (ev-5, ev-18, ev-20, ev-21). Slide also shows Investment deposits +1bpt (ev-19).

drivers.columns: FY20 vs FY21 (30 Jun 20 vs 30 Jun 21)
drivers.narrative: Lower business lending margins -1bpt from "repricing actions to support businesses during COVID-19", and consumer finance -1bpt from fewer interest-earning card balances (ev-4). Home lending margins were flat: repricing +9bpts offset by switching from variable to fixed rate loans -5bpts and increased competition/discounting -4bpts (ev-4, ev-15, ev-16, ev-17).

drivers.columns: FY20 vs FY21 (30 Jun 20 vs 30 Jun 21)
drivers.narrative: Lower earnings on Group capital "due to the falling interest rate environment" -3bpts, partly offset by a higher New Zealand contribution +1bpt reflecting lower wholesale funding costs and favourable portfolio mix, itself partly offset by RBNZ cash rate cuts (ev-9, ev-22, ev-23).

drivers.columns: FY20 vs FY21 (30 Jun 20 vs 30 Jun 21)
drivers.narrative: Favourable funding mix +4bpts from a higher average deposit funding ratio (77% at 30 Jun 21 vs 71% at 30 Jun 20), customers switching to at-call deposits and the TFF drawdown; partly offset by asset mix -2bpts on the decline in higher-margin consumer finance balances (ev-7, ev-28).

drivers.columns: FY20 vs FY21 (30 Jun 20 vs 30 Jun 21)
drivers.narrative: The spread between 3-month BBSW and 3-month OIS narrowed: margin rose 3bpts "reflecting a decrease in the average spread notwithstanding a structural reduction in exposure to basis risk" from growth in cash-rate-linked deposits and a mix shift towards fixed rate home loans (ev-8).

drivers.columns: FY20 vs FY21 (30 Jun 20 vs 30 Jun 21)
drivers.narrative: Increased margin by 2bpts "driven by higher bonds and commodities financing income in Global Markets" (ev-10) — consistent with the $3bn rise in average trading assets on higher commodities financing balances and government bond holdings (ev-6).

disagreements.topic: FY20 comparator NIM level / size of decline
disagreements.explanation: The FY21 KPI table prints both. The walk and the Group performance analysis are "Presented on a continuing operations basis", so the continuing-operations 2.07%->2.03% (-4bpts) is the framing that the bank's own decomposition explains (ev-24, ev-25, ev-11).

limitations: The bank qualifies the -4bpt liquids bar as having "Minimal impact on NII" (ev-12) and describes the margin as "Flat ex liquids" (ev-27): the headline decline is largely balance-sheet dilution from holding more low-yielding liquid assets, not lost earnings, so the -4bpts overstates the economic deterioration.

Sub-part figures inside the bars come from narrative/annotations and do not always tie exactly across documents: the results book prints deposit cash-rate impact as -7bpts while the slide annotation prints -8bpts (with Investment +1bpt), a presentational rounding/allocation difference within the same -3bpt net bar.
Both the adopted framing (results book narrative, pp.12-13) and the corroborating slide walk (p.63) use identical bar values, so no independent third quantification of the walk was available.

FY21 and FY20 average interest earning assets are net of mortgage offset balances and exclude assets held for sale, so the margin denominator basis differs from the gross balances printed in the accounts (ev-1 footnotes).

evidence_records.quote: Net interest margin (%) 2. 03 2. 07 (4)bpts 2. 04 2. 01 3 bpts

Net interest income was $18,839 million, an increase of $229 million or 1% on the prior year. The result was driven by a $32 billion or 4% increase in average interest earning assets to $930 billion, partly offset by a 4 basis point decrease in net interest margin to 2.03%.

The Bank’s net interest margin decreased 4 basis points on the prior year to 2.03%. The key drivers of the movement were: Liquid assets: Decreased margin by 4 basis points driven by increased lower yielding non-lending interest earning assets, including liquid assets.

numbers.label: Liquid assets contribution FY21 vs FY20

evidence_records.quote: Asset pricing: Decreased margin by 2 basis points driven by lower business lending margins (down 1 basis point) from repricing actions to support businesses during COVID-19, and lower consumer finance margins (down 1 basis point) from a reduction in the proportion of interest earning credit card balances. Home lending margins were flat, reflecting repricing (up 9 basis points), offset by the impact of customers switching from higher margin loans to lower margin loans, particularly from variable rate to fixed rate loans (down 5 basis points) and increased competition (down 4 basis points).

Funding costs: Decreased margin by 3 basis points, reflecting lower earnings on transaction and savings deposits mainly due to decreases in the cash rate (down 7 basis points), partly offset by higher benefits from the replicating portfolio (up 2 basis points) and lower wholesale funding costs (up 2 basis points).

numbers.label: Lower earnings on transaction and savings deposits (cash rate)

evidence_records.quote: Non-lending interest earning asset average balances increased $20 billion or 12% on the prior year to $195 billion, driven by a $17 billion increase in average liquid asset balances mainly due to strong customer deposit growth

Portfolio mix: Increased margin by 2 basis points driven by a higher average deposit funding ratio (30 June 2021: 77%; 30 June 2020: 71%) due to strong growth in transaction and savings deposits, customers switching to at-call deposits, and the drawdown of the TFF (up 4 basis points), partly offset by an unfavourable impact from asset mix (down 2 basis points), mainly due to a decline in higher margin consumer finance balances.

Basis risk: Basis risk arises from the spread between the 3 month bank bill swap rate and the 3 month overnight index swap rate. The Bank’s margin increased 3 basis points reflecting a decrease in the average spread notwithstanding a structural reduction in exposure to basis risk due to strong growth in cash rate linked deposits and a mix shift towards fixed rate home loans.

Capital and other: Decreased margin by 2 basis points driven by lower earnings on Group capital due to the falling interest rate environment (down 3 basis points), partly offset by increased contribution from New Zealand (up 1 basis point), reflecting lower wholesale funding costs and favourable portfolio mix, partly offset by the impact from RBNZ cash rate cuts.

numbers.label: Capital and other FY21 vs FY20

evidence_records.quote: Treasury and Markets: Increased margin by 2 basis points driven by higher bonds and commodities financing income in Global Markets.

numbers.label: Treasury and Markets FY21 vs FY20
